"... rationalism is a form of intellectual bigotry which, in thinking about reality, tries to take it into account as little as possible."

— José Ortega y Gasset

(Man and People, Ch. 6)

In the West's quest for the elucidation of Truth, logical operations have been invented as mechanistic implements to get to the bottom of things. In logic, the foundational pillars is that of Identity, Excluded Middle, and Non-Contradiction. The origin of Truth itself has been traditionally argued to be one of three principles of justification: infinite regress, circular (petitio principii), and self-evidence from first-principles. All of these have proven to have grievous issues, not the least of which applies to all of them at once, that is, the very methods used for unearthing "Truth" - this, "Identity", "Excluded Middle", and "Non-Contradiction" - are all held to be True in themselves, creating an absurd scenario where Truth loops its own loop.

But if we don't have this "Truth" that is detached and superior to ourselves, what do we make of these excellent implements of logical investigation? The answer is evident, yet strange at first sight. We take the concept of "Truth" and focus it in ourselves instead of in ethereal abstractions. This is far from saying that man is self-sufficient in an intellectual sense or otherwise. What I say is that Truth is no longer Truth qua abstract ideal, but a living verification within the vital and irrefutable reality of my life. In a sense, this is a return to first principles, but in a way much more severe than what a Plato or an Aristotle might have ever guessed. My life is the primary reality in a fundamental sense - not necessarily the most interesting or most important reality, but the reality on which every other reality depends on for its perception and other interactions with it.

In sum, my life is Truth, my epistemic horizon is my verification, and logical operations is how I sort out concepts and ideas I have of the world.
